subject: Residency guardrails & transient failover windows for NimbusPay
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@nimbuspay.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: NimbusPay Legal <legal@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 17:22:00 +0000
Subject: Residency guardrails and transient failover windows

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NimbusPay is excited about Redwood's performance. Before we proceed to a pilot, our security team needs clarity on two items that will affect the contract:

1) Cross-region transient processing: we need a clearly defined maximum window and list of triggers when requests or cached state may be processed outside APAC (e.g., scheduled maintenance, DR, soft failover). Can Redwood commit to a 6-hour maximum transient failover window and provide a list of automatic vs. manual triggers?

2) Subprocessors & KMS pathing: we require an exported subprocessor roster and confirmation that encrypted blobs remain within APAC KMS when region-pin is requested. If there are any short-lived paths that transit US/EU for indexing/analytics, we need scope and retention length.

Can you share a DPA addendum or a brief that we can circulate with our legal and cloud ops? Attached is our internal checklist (not exhaustive).

Thanks,
Amelia Torres
Director, IT Security
NimbusPay

Attachment: nimbus_checklist_security.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency guardrails and transient failover windows

Amelia — appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes we can document a bounded transient window and provide a subprocessor roster and KMS flow diagram.

High level proposal:
- Transient failover window: default automatic failover for customer-region pinning is bounded to 4 hours for automated short-term failovers (we aim for 30–90 minutes median). For extended maintenance or region evacuation the policy allows up to 24 hours with prior notice; however for NimbusPay we can commit to a contractual cap of 6 hours for automated failover in the DPA addendum.
- Triggers: automatic (node-level hardware failure, regional networking loss, autoscaler imbalance), manual (ops-initiated migrations, emergency DR). We'll provide a table mapping trigger -> expected max window -> notification SLAs.
- KMS and transient key material: data-at-rest remains encrypted and customer-managed keys (BYOK) can be pinned to APAC KMS; ephemeral indexing pipelines that require cross-region compute do not have access to raw plaintext and operate on hashed/derived telemetry only. We'll supply a diagram and the subprocessor roster.

I'll attach our draft DPA addendum and a short failover playbook for you to review. Laura — can Legal take the addendum and highlight any redlines to expect? Rishi — can you confirm the technical flow and whether the analytics path can be configured to keep all outputs within APAC if needed?

Best,
Michael
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_addendum_draft_v1.pdf; transient-failover-playbook.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@nimbuspay.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:36:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency guardrails and transient failover windows

Michael / Amelia — thanks for the outline. A few legal points up front for the DPA addendum draft:

- Contractual commitment: if we commit to a 6-hour max automated transient window, we should (a) define measurement points (start/end events), (b) include exceptions for force majeure and (c) offer a remediation SLA if breached (e.g., credits + post-incident remediation plan).
- KMS BYOK: we can offer KMS key import and APAC pinning, but we need to ensure customers accept responsibility for key lifecycle. We should include language that ephemeral replication for infrastructure reasons will not expose plaintext to subprocessors.
- Subprocessor roster: we'll produce the list but expect NimbusPay to request non-production subprocessor visibility (analytics vendors) and we'll need to mark which subprocessors touch metadata only vs. payload.

I attached an annotated addendum (DPA_addendum_draft_v1.pdf) and a proposed short set of SLAs. Amelia — legal asks: can you share a single page from NimbusPay legal stating minimum acceptable remediation for transient breaches (credits / escalation path)? That will speed review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (annotated)

From: NimbusPay Legal <legal@nimbuspay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@nimbuspay.com>, Evan Chu <evan.chu@cloudops.io>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency guardrails and transient failover windows

Laura / Michael — thanks for the draft. A few redlines from our side:

1) We appreciate the 6-hour cap but require a hard definition of "start" (first external routing outside APAC) and "end" (first successful response processed within APAC or verified KV sync).
2) Remediation: we propose a tiered credit schedule for breaches over the cap (6-12 hrs: 5% monthly credit; 12-24 hrs: 15%; >24 hrs: termination right after cure period).
3) Subprocessors: we need a commitment to 30 days' notice before adding analytics subprocessors that might touch derived telemetry, and an annual roster refresh with SOC2 attestation for any subprocessor that processes transaction metadata.

We'll attach our proposed redlines separately (legal_redlines_nimbus.docx). Evan (cloud ops) — will review the KMS flow and advise if temporary wrap keys passing through non-APAC compute is acceptable.

Regards,
NimbusPay Legal

Attachment: legal_redlines_nimbus.docx (attachment stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@nimbuspay.com>, NimbusPay Legal <legal@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency guardrails and transient failover windows

Amelia / team — quick technical summary and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view:

- Measurement: start = first request routed to non-APAC compute OR first KV cache miss triggering remote fetch; end = last sequence for which the producing node confirms APAC-local persist & KV reconciliation completed. We'll provide a deterministic event log schema for this in the next 24 hours.
- KMS: for NimbusPay pilot we will enable customer-managed keys pinned to the APAC KMS cluster. Any temporary wrap keys used during routing will be generated and destroyed < 1 hour; they will never carry plaintext and will be logged.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (subprocessor_roster_aug2026.csv). Items marked "metadata-only" do not access request payloads. Non-production analytics pipelines are currently optional; we can disable them for the pilot or add contractual notice.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to update DPA addendum with (a) 6-hour automated failover cap, (b) measurement definition and event log schema, (c) remediation credits language proposal (Laura to draft).
2) NimbusPay legal to return redlines against the addendum.
3) Ops sync (Rishi + Evan + Grace) to run a short runbook against a simulated node failure — target Friday 20 Aug.

I'll queue the updated artifacts to the Drive link noted below and share the runbook with your ops contact.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_aug2026.csv; transient-failover-playbook.docx (updated)
